newsitem.title: DUBAI: Normal start to Saudi stock market trade.
newsitem.headline: Normal start to Saudi stock market trade.

text.p: Trade in Saudi Arabian shares started as normal on Sunday after problems with its computerised trading system in the past few days, traders said on Sunday.
"The market opened on time today. It is back to normal," a trader said by telephone from Riyadh.
There was no trade on Thursday when the kingdom's Electronic Securities Information System was down. On Saturday trade started 90 minutes late after technical problems.
The Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency said in a statement carried by Saudi newspapers the failure was due to "disruption in the hypothetical certificates processor".
The Saudi Gazette said this was the second stoppage in ESIS in two months. The first lasted for 30 minutes.
The Saudi market is open from 10.00 a.m. to noon (0700 GMT to 0900 GMT) and from 4.25 p.m. to 6.30 p.m. (1325 GMT to 1530 GMT) Saturday to Thursday.
